comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Second ask, Chat Notes 2026-10-14 (voice): "Viewing at human messages is still super awkward. It opens up like a new pane and there's just plain text, it's hard to parse. I think there's already an outstanding ticket for this but this needs to be properly implemented via some other approach." Going to a message notification today opens a pane running `muster msg log --follow` (docs/architecture.md, attention routing).

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Committed 2026-10-16, after the second ask. First step: draft a MIP for the view (native AppKit over a core view-model, or a richer terminal view) and how membership shows on rows.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Mockups, 2026-10-24: Lectern artifact muster-group-conversation. Recommended direction: a native drawer over the panes (A), with a queue of everything waiting on you (B) and banner/sidebar replies (C) as later additions. Agreed in its thread for the MIP: the conversation shows each member's pane state, including a turn that ended without a post, and muster docs msg states plainly how each channel reaches the human. Which channel an agent uses stays the user's skills' call, not Muster's. Open in the MIP: Markdown parsed in the core or in Swift; answers an agent offers as buttons (a new message field).

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Agreed on the mockups since (muster-group-conversation v3): a message that starts with @ and a member's name addresses that member in place of the default recipient, and an @ later only completes the name; only the composer reads it, and msg post keeps --to. Answers an agent offers fill the reply instead of sending it, so a note can go with them; the reply carries the choice as text for the agent and as a field for Muster. Unsent replies are kept per group on the daemon, with the human's participant, and the sidebar row marks a waiting draft.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Direction changed in muster-group-conversation v4, replacing the drawer: choosing a group (sidebar row or banner) shows its conversation in place of the panes until Esc or a tab or pane is chosen; a members column gives each agent Go to pane. Any window can show any group, two at once included; each window's message box and draft are its own (kept with the window's saved arrangement, not the daemon), and a post shows in both. Keep the door open to a conversation pane in a tab's tree later (a pane with no terminal, a protocol change). Terms: group, conversation, message box, transcript (the msg log pane), Needs you, banner. A banner with a reply field and offered answers is the first piece to ship.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Owner approved the design in muster-group-conversation v4 (2026-10-24). This card stays the conversation view itself, whose next step is the MIP. Split out as children: a_2naAacfIB (banner shows the message and takes a reply; ship first), a_2naAat73L (answers an agent offers), a_2naAbBoP6 (msg docs on how each channel reaches the human), a_2naAbSaGZ (Needs you queue), a_2naAbjFtA (conversation as a pane, uncommitted). Naming: B's queue is "Needs you" on screen and "asking" in code and CLI.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Codex critique (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh), 2026-10-24, claims spot-checked against the code. For the MIP: (1) Showing the conversation in place of the panes must change what the core counts as on screen, not only what Swift draws. Attention::seen is window focus plus the visible-pane set (crates/muster-core/src/attention.rs:748), and a transcript somebody is looking at reads new messages for the human (crates/muster-seam/src/session.rs:6563). If only the shell hides the surfaces, a covered terminal finishes unseen and loses its done, and a covered transcript reads messages nobody saw. Publish covered panes as not on screen, and restore real focus on the way back. Both need headless checks; Esc during input-method composition needs a native one. (2) Send has four outcomes, not two: pending, saved (with whom it woke, or nobody live: exit 6), refused, and unknown (a remote post can be appended and still answer unanswered: exit 4). MsgRequest.Post has no idempotency key, so never retry an unknown post automatically, and keep the text on refusal or doubt. (3) Default recipient must be someone who can be addressed: @muster is never a valid addressee (crates/muster-msg/src/names.rs), and an author who left the group is refused. (4) Keep a draft whole: recipients, urgency, picked answer and text, keyed by window and group; a message arriving must not retarget it. (5) Share one history cache per group across windows, fetched incrementally with Log since=N, rather than each window re-reading the log (bodies up to 1 MiB).

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Owner, 2026-10-24: nothing in this work is answered through a macOS notification. Muster draws its own banner in the window (Swift, SwiftUI), for the reason MIP-3 replaced herdr: "the more vertically integrated we are, the better an experience we can deliver with Muster." The banner card a_2naAacfIB is rewritten to match. Open: whether a message still raises a macOS notification, as a pointer back to Muster only, while Muster is not in front.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Settled by the owner, 2026-10-24: while Muster is not in front, a message for the human still raises a macOS notification, as a pointer back to Muster only. It carries no reply field and no answers; choosing it brings Muster forward to the message. Everything else is answered in Muster's own banner and conversation.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
amterp, Chat Notes 2026-10-07: "GUI for following groups". Clarified 2026-10-07: following a group today means a tab running `muster msg log --follow`, which is "a very plain text file. It's really hard to parse ... not really easy to understand and follow. It's not really a GUI either for contributing back to the discussion in a way that others can see. Like you still have to talk to the agents directly. There's no way for me to kind of like talk in the group and have that be broadcast through muster." "It's a pretty big feature ... might require some design input."

And a related wish, same day: "if you have agents that work together in a group, it would be nice in the UI to have some sort of way to see what groups are active and which panes are involved in which groups, like some sort of visualization."

So two parts: a group conversation view that reads well (authors, addressees, urgency, joins and leaves) with a place for the human to post into the group; and an overview of active groups and which panes are in each. Needs a MIP: native AppKit view over a core view-model versus a richer terminal view, and how membership shows on panes and agent-list rows.
title: 💬 A group conversation you can read and post into, and a view of which panes are in which groups
